label: Multiplayer Sync
title: Multiplayer sync
lead: KrokMP compatibility: automatic sync for registered content, plus a host-authoritative snapshot and message API.
bodyHtml:
Wait, what?

CUCoreLib has a soft compatibility layer for Casualties: Together

This is split into two main sections:

  • Content - custom items, buildings, tiles and liquids you registered through CUCoreLib resolve over C:T's own object sync, so a peer can spawn your content, with all item data that exists inside CUCoreLib's registries.
  • State - CUCoreLib runs its own host-authoritative snapshot on top of KrokMP's transport, plus a request and message API for your traffic.

For registered content and registry-backed state you write no multiplayer code at all. Everything below is the part you must write with (using) CUCoreLib.Networking.MultiplayerApi.

How state moves

KrokMP is host-authoritative, and so is CUCoreLib's sync layer. That is, the host owns the truth, and clients pull it:

  • A connecting client requests the full snapshot once (cucorelib.sync.snapshot) and applies every module in it. If it lands while the client is not in a world, CUCoreLib caches it and replays it once you are in one.

What you get for free (automatically!)

CUCoreLib registers its built-in snapshot modules during startup. Anything you put through the normal registries is already covered.

Note that the client does *not* need your mod (only CUCoreLib) for basic functionality, but will need it for any custom logic or content.

Module keyWhat crosses the wire
itemsCustom item definitions: e.g. names, descriptions, category, sprites, wearable flags, weight and condition behaviour.
liquidsCustom liquid definitions: e.g. colour, value per litre, injection and usability flags, crafting qualities.
lootpoolsLoot pool contents and weights, so world loot matches the host.
tilesCustom block definitions.
liquidtilesLiquid tile definitions.
buildingsCustom building entity definitions.
moodlesCustom moodle definitions.
settingsRegistered mod options and their values.
 
ItemRegistry.Register("conicalFlask", flaskInfo, flaskSprite);
// This will automatically have multiplayer support, alongside most custom fields ^
BuildingEntityRegistry.Register("SporeMine", new CustomBuildingEntityDefinition
{
    Name = "Spore mine",
    Sprite = sporeMineSprite,
    Components = new[] { typeof(SporeMineScript) }
}); // Every peer gets a spore mine.
    // HOWEVER, its custom SporeMineScript logic is yours, and is not synced UNLESS both users have the mod that adds said spore mine.

What is not automatic: your own MonoBehaviour logic, state you keep outside the registries, and anything you change after a peer pulled its snapshot. Those need a sync module or a message, below.

Messages and requests

The public surface is CUCoreLib.Networking.MultiplayerApi, so a dependent mod never has to reflect into KrokMP internals.

You shouldn't be doing that regardless if you can help it, as you'd be needing to potentially update your mod per multiplayer update. (instead, delegate the work to me ;) )

Anyhow, non-abstracted payloads arrive as a JToken, and every send returns false instead of throwing when the bridge is not there. Channels are plain strings, compared case-sensitively, so do namespace them (mymod.kiln.setmode).

APIUse it for
IsAvailableWhether the CUCoreLib bridge found KrokMP and installed its receivers. False with no KrokMP, or on a build whose signatures it could not match.
IsRunning, IsClient, IsServer, IsHostRole checks before server-only or client-only work.
KrokMpVersionThe installed KrokMP version, or null when it is not loaded.
RegisterServerHandlerClient-to-server traffic. Return a JToken to answer a request, or null for fire-and-forget events.
RegisterClientHandlerServer-to-client events.
RegisterHandlerThe same one-way handler on clients and the server, no response.
SendToServerClient one-way event to the host.
RequestServerClient request with a response callback.
SendToClientServer event to one client ID.
BroadcastServer event to every client. The host is skipped unless includeHost: true.
BroadcastEverywhereAn event on every instance in the lobby, including your own, from any role - the host relays for clients. This is the one for "everyone sees this".
BroadcastToPeerAn event on one instance, whichever role you hold, including client to client through the host. An unknown client ID returns false.
SendToPeerSends to the chosen client when called on the server, and to the server when called on a client. Note: it never relays between clients! Use BroadcastEverywhere and BroadcastToPeer for that.
RegisterSyncModuleYour own durable state inside the shared snapshot.
CaptureSnapshot, ApplySnapshotBuild or consume a snapshot by hand.
BroadcastSnapshotHost push of the current full snapshot to every client.
RequestInitialSnapshotClient re-pull, when something changed that only otherwise lands on join.
GetCustomPlayerData, GetCustomPlayerLimbDataServer-side read of one player's custom body or limb statuses.
RequestCustomPlayerData, RequestCustomPlayerLimbDataThe same, from a client.

Registration is startup-only. Register them from Awake like any other registry.

Using JObject

A JObject is just a small JSON-style bundle of values. Use it when one side needs to ask the other side a question.

In this example the client asks whether a feature is unlocked, and the server sends back one value: unlocked.

This example is the most flexible form. For the majority of modders, using CUCoreLib's abstracted functions, as shown on the right side code pane, may be more convenient.

using CUCoreLib.Networking;
using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq;
using UnityEngine;

private void Awake()
{
    // This runs on the server when a client asks this question.
    MultiplayerApi.RegisterServerHandler("mymod.is-feature-unlocked", request =>
    {
        string featureId = request?.Value<string>("featureId");
        bool unlocked = featureId == "challenge-mode";

        return new JObject
        {
            ["unlocked"] = unlocked
        };
    });
}

private void AskServerIfGlassworksIsUnlocked()
{
    MultiplayerApi.RequestServer(
        "mymod.is-feature-unlocked",
        new JObject
        {
            ["featureId"] = "challenge-mode"
        },
        response =>
        {
            bool unlocked = response?.Value<bool?>("unlocked") ?? false;

            if (unlocked)
            {
                Debug.Log("Challenge mode is unlocked!");
            }
        }
    );
}

RegisterServerHandler answers the question, RequestServer asks it, and JObject is the note passed between them.

For a machine whose mode the host decides, the same pair runs in reverse on the way back: the client requests a change, the server validates it, applies it, and Broadcasts the accepted value to everyone.

Custom snapshot modules

Use MultiplayerApi.RegisterSyncModule when your mod owns shared state that no registry covers: discovered markers, machine recipes, per-world unlocks, cached server decisions. A module is one capture callback and, optionally, one apply callback.

This should look familiar from the Saving API. It uses the same shape, except snapshots cross the network instead :)

using CUCoreLib.Networking;
using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq;

private readonly Dictionary<string, Vector2> markers = new Dictionary<string, Vector2>();

private void Awake()
{
    MultiplayerApi.RegisterSyncModule(
        "glassworks.markers",
        CaptureMarkerSnapshot,
        ApplyMarkerSnapshot
    );
}

private JObject CaptureMarkerSnapshot()
{
    JObject root = new JObject();
    foreach (KeyValuePair<string, Vector2> marker in markers)
    {
        root[marker.Key] = new JObject
        {
            ["x"] = marker.Value.x,
            ["y"] = marker.Value.y
        };
    }

    return root;
}

private void ApplyMarkerSnapshot(JObject snapshot)
{
    if (snapshot == null) return;

    markers.Clear();
    foreach (JProperty property in snapshot.Properties())
    {
        JObject marker = property.Value as JObject;
        if (marker == null) continue;

        markers[property.Name] = new Vector2(
            marker.Value<float?>("x") ?? 0f,
            marker.Value<float?>("y") ?? 0f
        );
    }
}

Statuses, per player

Your own custom statuses already sync: every client asks the host for its own body snapshot once a second, and the host answers from the sender's body, so one player's effects can never overwrite another's. No code needed.

Reading somebody else's statuses is a request. Use KrokMP's clientId to choose which player body to read - a clientId is the multiplayer player ID, not the display name.

GetCustomPlayerData returns that player's custom BodyStatus payloads, GetCustomPlayerLimbData their custom LimbStatus payloads, and the Request... pair is the client-side version of the same read.

// Ask the server for one player's custom body statuses.
MultiplayerApi.RequestCustomPlayerData(clientId, response =>
{
    JArray bodyStatuses = response?["body"] as JArray;
    Debug.Log("Body status payloads: " + (bodyStatuses?.Count ?? 0));
});

// Ask the server for one player's custom limb statuses.
MultiplayerApi.RequestCustomPlayerLimbData(clientId, response =>
{
    JArray limbStatuses = response?["limbs"] as JArray;
    Debug.Log("Limb status payloads: " + (limbStatuses?.Count ?? 0));
});
